rows.whyFourArtifactsAndNotTwo: CR-65 Rev. 10/2024 prints the trafficking ground twice, once under each Alabama statute: Section I option 8 (Check Box9.0, § 15-27-1(a)(8), misdemeanor charge) and Section III option 8 (Check Box10.4, § 15-27-2(a)(8), felony charge). The form says "Check ONLY one (1) of the eight (8) options" and "Only one offense per petition", and the record defers the choice to the offence level rather than fixing it — the worklist deliverable reads "Petition under the applicable subsection" and the compiled runtime profile says "Two statutes (misdemeanor § 15-27-1, felony § 15-27-2)" and "Then pick § 15-27-1 (misdemeanor)". Shipping only one subsection would deliver half the route; switching subsection between canonical and boundary would make the pair incomparable. So each subsection gets its own canonical and boundary, which is the shape az_marijuana_expungement_arrest_no_charges-set already ships.

findingsForTheCaptain.finding: STRATEGY LABEL DISAGREEMENT — MASTER_QUEUE.json and packet-family-build-worklist.json both label al-trafficking-set custom_pleading. AL.memo.json track al-trafficking records outputStrategy official_pdf_fill, gives all three components an officialFormId (CR-65, CR-65, C-10-CRIMINAL), and states "The route uses the same official CR-65 petition as the other Alabama tracks"; its legalDesignDecision says the amendment "expressly changes the output strategy from process_guidance". Built as the controlling legal record directs, because composing a pleading while the record directs an official form would be a source-fidelity defect. Recorded in approval-request.json under strategyRecordDisagreement and not resolved here. The overlay directory keeps the assignment's --custom-pleading suffix because that is the path PF06 owns; the completeness verifier reads family identity from approval-request.json, so discovery is unaffected.

OPEN OWNER SCOPING QUESTION — CR-65 Section IV (Check Box10.5, Ala. Code § 15-27-2(b)) is the narrow exception letting a trafficking survivor reach a CONVICTION for one of three enumerated violent felonies. AL.memo.json cites § 15-27-2(b) among the track's authorities; the worklist deliverable names only §§ 15-27-1(a)(8) / 15-27-2(a)(8), and Section IV is a conviction branch rather than a charge branch. Not elected, refused by name in the field map, and disclosed to the participant. Whether this family covers it is an owner determination and was not guessed.

UNBOUND COMPANION — the compiled Alabama runtime profile states "The petition is accompanied by a proposed Order of Expungement (§ 15-27-6)". The worklist records this family's proposedOrder as not_recorded, AL.memo.json's component list carries none, and no official Alabama order binary is bound to the family. No order was invented; the gap is named in the participant guide and surfaced here.

RELEASE BLOCKER ALREADY ON THE RECORD — AL.memo.json track al-trafficking carries unresolvedQuestions: "Current official text of Ala. Code §§ 15-27-3, 15-27-5, and 15-27-12 has not been read", impact release_blocker, affectedElement governing_mechanism. Under the build-first review model this gates approved_for_live, not state_built, so it did not block this build. Carried forward so it is not lost at promotion.

OBSERVED ON A SIBLING, NOT REPAIRED BY PF06 — the shared Alabama host scripts/build-census-v1-al-diversion-set.mjs writes reports/actual-writes.json with addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes: 0 and nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes: 0 as literals and flattenedWidgetAppearancesReadFromOutputBytes from packet.writes.length, none of which reads output bytes despite the field names. PF06 did not touch that host or those families: they are outside PF06's owned paths and belong to other lanes.

rows.whyStopClassDiffersFromTheBuilderAtBase: The builder at the base commit classifies this refusal BLOCKED_SOURCE. PF06 reproduced its measurement and reclassifies it BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT, because all four sources bind by exact SHA-256 and the assignment defines BLOCKED_SOURCE as a family whose source does not bind. What is missing is not bytes; it is a determination about which court this family files in, and therefore which court-specific edition of the fee-waiver forms applies, or authority to drop the fee-waiver pair. That is an owner determination PF06 must not guess and must not research.
rows.openLegalInput: New Hampshire publishes court-specific editions of these forms, and this family binds a Superior Court fee-waiver motion beside a Circuit Court petition and a Circuit Court financial statement. The owner must decide one of: (a) bind the Circuit Court edition of NHJB-2311 matching NHJB-3057-DSe and NHJB-2328-DFPe; (b) bind the Superior Court edition of the financial statement and scope this family to Superior Court annulments; or (c) determine that the fee-waiver components may be dropped and replaced by a pointer to whichever fee-waiver forms the filing court actually uses.

measuredIndependentlyFromTheBoundBytes.how: The three binaries were loaded directly from the Master Library at their pinned digests and every court dropdown's FULL option list was read — not only the Superior-court subset the builder at base filters on — so the intersection reported here is over all options, not a filtered view.
measuredIndependentlyFromTheBoundBytes.consequence: No New Hampshire court can be named on both fee-waiver components, and neither offers a free-text court field. Scoping does not rescue it: scoping to Superior Court leaves NHJB-2328 unable to name the court, and scoping to Circuit Court leaves NHJB-2311 unable to. Filling NHJB-2311 for a Circuit Court annulment delivers the wrong court's motion; leaving its court blank delivers a motion that does not say where it is filed.
measuredIndependentlyFromTheBoundBytes.noAlternativeEditionIsHeld: The entire Master Library holds exactly one NHJB-2311 and exactly one NHJB-2328, so unblocking options (a) and (b) both additionally require a source that is not in custody here. This is new measurement: the builder at base did not record it.

rows.whyNoPartialBuildWasShipped: The builder contract requires every component the route names, and a document mapped but not rendered is a missing companion form. Shipping two of four would read as built. The assignment also requires a stopped family to leave its overlay directory byte-for-byte unchanged; this one was never created.
rows.secondFindingCarriedForward: NHJB-2956 prints "PURPOSE OF RECORD: Housing / Employment / Annulment/Expungement / Other ______" and draws no control beside the printed options — no AcroForm widget and no stroked box, only printed words and white space. The route's own identity answers the question, but the only writable control on that line is the "Other" rule, and writing the purpose there would state that the purpose is Other, which is false. Whether the packet may mark it is an owner determination.
